labels.zh-CN: 最后一周量占峰值比例

details.formulaDescription: Validate raceDistance against 5k/10k/half/marathon/ultra; peakWeeklyKm greater than zero; peakLongRunKm not negative; qualitySessionsPerWeek between 1 and 3; taperWeeks 2 or 3; daysToRace between 0 and 28. Three-week volume ratios are 0.80, 0.60, 0.40 and long-run ratios 0.85, 0.65, 0.45. Two-week volume ratios are 0.70, 0.45 and long-run ratios 0.70, 0.50. Quality sessions: with one weekly session the plan is 1,1,0 (three weeks) or 1,1 (two weeks); with two or three it is 2,2,1 (three weeks) or 2,1 (two weeks). Week volume = round(peakWeeklyKm * volumeRatio); week long run = round(peakLongRunKm * longRunRatio). taperRatio = round1(last raw weekly volume / peakWeeklyKm * 100). intensityRetention is maintained: session distance and rep count shorten while target pace stays unchanged. Warnings: daysToRace below taperWeeks * 7 reports a taper window too short; marathon with peakWeeklyKm below 30 reports a low peak-volume reference; both join into one warning string.
assumptions: The plan assumes the peak week already delivered by the runner; it does not prescribe how to reach that peak.
Quality pace remains at target race or threshold pace; reduced volume does not mean slower pace.
Ratios are group-level planning heuristics from endurance tapering research, not an individual physiological prescription.
The tool does not schedule strength work, mobility, sleep, nutrition or carbohydrate loading.
Ultra and trail events may need longer tapering depending on cumulative fatigue and vertical load; the 2-3 week range is a starting point.
details.rounding: Weekly volume and long-run km round to the nearest whole kilometre; taperRatio keeps one decimal; ratios are applied to raw peak values before rounding.
